messages:
Maria G: customer Brightleaf on dedicated pool eu-west-2 reporting intermittent p99 spikes ~3x normal and occasional 429s. started after yesterday's autoscale bump. ticket #BR-4389. can infra take a look?
Sofia L: ack — can you paste a short repro and the pool id?
Maria G: pool: eu2-dedicated-56, tenant brightleaf-prod. quick repro: steady chat generation at 8 rps, seq len ~1024. after ~20m, p99 jumps and some requests return 429 throttle. we saw process-level GPU utilization still <70%. logs attached (snippet):
```
2025-05-29T14:22:03Z INFO request id=abc123 tokens=512 latency=42ms
2025-05-29T14:27:41Z WARN request id=def456 p99=1280ms status=200
2025-05-29T14:28:02Z ERROR request id=ghi789 status=429 reason="server_throttle"
```
Sofia L: interesting. 429 says server side throttle triggered. did autoscaler mark node as draining or evicting slices?
Maria G: autoscale logs show a transient scale-down a few mins earlier, then immediate scale-up. scale-down reason: low cpu on host, but GPU slices were still busy.
Raj P: that smells like fractional MIG packing + eviction race. when we compact slices we sometimes push KV cache churn and evict tasks leading to tail latency. can we get the gpuslice mapping and MIG config for the node id?
Alice T: grabbing node and slice info now — node n-eu2-1124. MIG layout: 1g.10gb + 2g.20gb mixed (customer requested mixed sizing). slices pinned: brightleaf had 2 slices on same host alongside small batch jobs from other tenants.
Maria G: other tenants on same node were low-priority batch workers, but we saw spikes align with their nightly batch kickoffs.
Sofia L: hypotheses: 1) KV cache eviction when slices consolidate during scale-change 2) PCIe or L3 thrash when batch jobs peak 3) autoscaler heuristics using host CPU causing misdecisions.
Raj P: to repro, we should: 1) run synthetic steady stream at similar token patterns toward brightleaf slice 2) trigger autoscaler to scale-down/up by simulating low cpu on host 3) run a co-located batch job hitting all SMs to mimic neighbor noise. I'll prepare a repro job.
Maria G: can you include the exact commands? support needs to run minimal steps in customer lab to reproduce.
Raj P: sample steps (run from infra bastion):
```
# steady generator
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -H "Authorization: Bearer $BRIGHTLEAF_KEY" -d '{"model":"rwd-medu-13b","input":"<long prompt>","max_tokens":512,"rate":8}' &
# trigger scale-down (force host CPU low) — simulation only
kubectl patch node n-eu2-1124 -p '{"metadata":{"annotations":{"test/force-cpu":"low"}}}'
# start neighbor batch (on same node via affinity)
kubectl run noise-batch --image=gpustress:1 --overrides='{"spec":{"affinity":{"nodeAffinity":{"requiredDuringSchedulingIgnoredDuringExecution":{"nodeSelectorTerms":[{"matchExpressions":[{"key":"kubernetes.io/hostname","operator":"In","values":["n-eu2-1124"]}]}]}}}}' -- /bin/stress-gpu --util 90
```
Alice T: I copied the commands to a reproducibility job job-id repro-1758. will run in staging eu2 cluster and report metrics.
OpsBot: scheduled job repro-1758 on staging-eu2 at 2025-05-29T16:05:00Z.
SupportEngine: FYI customer-facing note: told Brightleaf we're investigating; recommend reducing aggressive scale-down window until we confirm.
Sofia L: next steps: Raj to run repro and capture per-slice GPU metrics (SM util, memory bw, pci-e counters), Maria to ask Brightleaf to hold off scale-down policy change, Alice to collect node packing snapshot + autoscaler events.
Raj P: running now, will post results in ~20m. initial thought: if KV cache churn is culprit we should see large host memory copies and increased CPU sys time during consolidation.
Maria G: thanks — please drop any sample flame graphs or nvtop screenshots. I'll update the customer. :thumbsup:
Sofia L: if repro succeeds we'll propose: 1) change autoscaler to consider GPU queue depth, not just host cpu, 2) prefer draining whole host vs fractional compaction during active low-latency tenants, 3) blackout neighbor batch scheduling windows for ded pools.
Maria G: noted. tagging @brightleaf-engineering will coordinate later.
